subject: Cloud Computing
title: DDoS Protection
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on DDoS Protection.

hook.text: Millions of fake requests flood your server. It drowns under the load. That's a DDoS attack.

buildup.text: Distributed Denial of Service attacks overwhelm targets with traffic from thousands of compromised machines.

discovery.text: Cloud providers offer built-in DDoS protection. AWS Shield, Azure DDoS Protection, and Cloud Armor absorb attacks.

twist.text: The cloud's massive scale is actually an advantage here. It can absorb traffic volumes no single server could.

climax.text: DDoS attacks are getting larger every year. The biggest recorded attack exceeded 71 million requests per second.

punchline.text: DDoS attacks flood. Cloud scale absorbs. Size is defense.

quiz.question: Why is the cloud well-suited to defend against DDoS attacks?
options: Its massive scale can absorb traffic volumes no single server could handle
Cloud servers are immune to receiving network traffic
DDoS attacks only target on-premises servers, not cloud

details.summary: DDoS attacks flood cloud resources with traffic to overwhelm availability. Cloud providers offer built-in DDoS protection that absorbs volumetric attacks, and advanced tiers add automatic detection and mitigation for application-layer attacks.
details.whyItMatters: Even cloud-scale infrastructure can be degraded by large DDoS attacks. Built-in and advanced protections keep services available during attacks without manual intervention.
takeaways: Cloud providers include basic DDoS protection at no extra cost
Advanced tiers protect against sophisticated application-layer attacks
CDNs and auto-scaling help absorb attack traffic

faq.question: How large can DDoS attacks get?
faq.answer: Record attacks have exceeded 3 terabits per second. Cloud providers can absorb these volumetric attacks because their global networks have far more capacity than any single customer. The greater challenge today is low-volume application-layer attacks that mimic legitimate traffic.

faq.question: Does auto-scaling protect against DDoS?
faq.answer: Auto-scaling can absorb some traffic spikes but can also dramatically increase costs during an attack. Purpose-built DDoS protection identifies and drops malicious traffic before it reaches your resources, avoiding both downtime and runaway scaling bills.
